segments.text: Vidya samutthane saabhavike kechiri ishwavasta, saabhavike samutthane, saabhavike without any effort, shuddh vidya,
then at the rise of shuddh vidya, shuddh vidya means pure knowledge of eye consciousness or God consciousness.
Pure knowledge of God consciousness rises naturally without any effort and kechiri ishwavasta.
This state of shiva is realized, which is one with the state of kejiri.
Kejiri, kejiri avasta, state of kejiri or state of shiva.
Praaak nirdishta satatva vidya saabhavike samutthane,
this shuddh vidya, this pure knowledge which has already been explained previously, in previous sutras.
When that pure knowledge comes into existence without any effort, saabhavike.
Paramesh ishya matra gatite mith siddh nekhbhavini sahaja samujane, samun majjane,
when by the supreme divine will of Lord Shiva, Paramesh ishya matra gatite,
by the supreme individual will of Lord Shiva, mith siddh nekhbhavini,
these limited powers are subsided and sahaja samujane,
and that real state of Lord Shiva comes into being.
Then what happens ke bodhagavine charati di kejiri,
he roams and flies in the ether of knowledge, supreme knowledge,
in the akasha of supreme knowledge, that is kejiri mutra,
that abhivajjate, that comes into existence for him.
And this state of kejiri is shiva siya chitnaathaseya.
This is the state of Lord Shiva, who is chitnaathaseya,
who is the supreme embodiment of consciousness,
and who is avasthata o sambhani, who is one with the sadhaka.
Sadhaka becomes one with that Shiva and so on and uchalata ropa.
This is the way of rise of one's own blissful state.
This is not kejiri, as said in these two shlokas,
Bhaddha padmasanam yogi nabhav akhe sharam neset.
Just be seated in padmasana, when yogi is seated in padmasana,
and he puts his mind, akhe sharam means, the master of all organs.
The master of all organs is mind.
All organs are directed towards the mind.
By mind, and he puts his mind, he must put his mind in the center of navel, navi.
Dandhaka amdhutavattat, and he must sit erect, not bend his body.
Nayat yavat kakhatrayam, to that point, when three ethers come into existence for him.
Three ethers are shakti, vahapini and samana.
Shakti, vahapini and samana are already explained previously in previous sutras.
And then, imagedly yogi nikrehe ta turam.
Turnam means, imagedly.
Imagedly, yogi should infuse, supreme wired.
That supreme wiredness should be infused by yogi by taking hold of three wired.
That is, shakti, vahapini and samana.
Etam baddha maha yogi, khe gatim prityapattati.
By doing this way, yogi enters in the mudra of kechari.
This kechari mudra is not meant here.
This kechari mudra should be avoided.
It should be neglected.
Nathu ye tevamsamsthane viseesha anasarna rupa.
This is not real kechari mudra.
What is real kechari mudra? Abhitu.
Param's gatim eti arthabhave na kulamarge na nittisha,
charate sarvjantu nam kechari namasasamrata.
But when by holding the way of totality, kulamarge na,
you must hold the way of totality.
See total totality in part, take one part of universe
and see the whole universe existing there.
That is the way of totality.
You must understand that everything is complete.
Everything is filled with completion.
If only one being is there, one individual being,
you must understand and you must feel that in one individual being,
all individuals exist.
Just as a grain of some bird paddy or wheat or one grain,
see the power in that grain, how much power exists in that one grain?
Not power of producing hundred plants,
not thousand, not millions, not billions.
Univariable plants are there existing in one grain of paddy.
And they buy and buy, they produce so many plants.
So, one part of the world is complete in itself.
So, you must when by holding the way of totality,
this is the way of holding totality in each and every being.
One feels, awareness of differentiated perceptions.
In each and every being, that is real.
In real sense, that is Kajari.
That Kajari, Kajari Mudra should be practised.
It is the Tantrasadva in a group with a person with this rupa.
So, this Kajari Mudra is just as is said in Tantrasadva,
becoming one with supreme consciousness.
Even if you have a Vedatma-kumayi,
samastra-klob-prasantya,
then all differentiated way of the energy of illusion of Lord Shiva.
I mean, the agitation of that differentiated illusion of Lord Shiva
comes to an end.
When that ends, that differentiated illusion ends.
That agitation, chob-prasantya,
that comes into nothingness.
Chidātma-kusuru-bhunma-janay-kuru-pa-mantri-virya-mudra-virya-jaya-distam.
Then here, the power of all mantras and the power of all states is explained.
And got into experience.
Mantra-virya is the power of all mantras.
Mudra-virya is the power of all states.
The power of all states and the power of all mantras appears to such yogis.
This is said in Kulchūdha-mani-sastra.
Akaṁ śrītmāyaṁ bijaṁ aka-mudra-jī-khe-chiri.
When one germ of one germ of creative being and one germ of existence,
first it is created.
First that mudra is created, then it is established.
Creation is mantra-virya.
Establishment is mudra-virya.
Dāvētav-jaya-ditya.
These two states, to whom appear?
Soti-shānta-pade-esita.
He is established in that supreme peaceful state of Lord Shiva.
Sbandhya-to-mantra-virya-sorup-nirupane-naiva-mudra-viryaṁ sangrihitam.
In Sbandhya, mudra-virya also is narrated in the explanation of mantra-virya.
So there is no difference between mantra-virya and mudra-virya.
Mantra-virya is only the beginning of creative energy,
and establishment in that creative energy is mudra-virya.
Yadā-tova-prili-yadadāsya-param-padam.
When all these agitations and then this state of Lord Shiva comes into being.
Ani-parena-pi.
If this shloka of Sbandhya is explained in other, for other subjects.
But this also is hinted.
This mantra-virya and mudra-virya is hinted in this shloka.
